Subject: PrivGPU loadshape profiling + network path inspection

Hi Aditi / BrightLane infra team,

Thanks for the staged handoff earlier. We ran a short synthetic storm against the private GPU pool last night and saw a few curious patterns: bursts that aligned with specific client prefixes, and intermittent 10-30ms latency spikes between the gateway and the first NIC on the inference hosts. Before we schedule a longer soak, can you do two things:

1) Share the recent packet path traces for the cluster (ingress -> egress) so we can validate RTT + MTU behavior; a pcap extract for a representative 10-minute window is ideal.
2) Confirm whether any network ACLs or middleboxes (WAF, L7 balancer) are doing per-request inspection and whether they have a burst/inspection concurrency limit.

Attached: sample loadshape CSV (3 bins) describing the synthetic qps mix we used.

Goal: we want to bake a reliable headroom curve for private GPU pools that accounts for network-bound stalls. If you can send the traces and a quick note on inspection points by EOD tomorrow, we can combine with our profiling math and propose scaling thresholds.

Thanks,
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Hi Stephanie — thanks for the clear note.

Quick answers:
- I've attached a trimmed pcap for 2027-04-02 22:00-22:10 UTC (netdiag-path-trace.pcap). It includes the gateway->host handoff and our L4 balancer health-checks.
- We don't have an active L7 proxy in the path for the test cluster (we route direct to the inference frontends). However, the security team has a passive packet inspector that samples ~1% of traffic and occasionally triggers cpu-stealing in the NIC offload path when it sees large frames. We're opening a ticket to exclude the test VLAN from sampling during soak runs.

Notes from cursory glance: there are several 1500->9000 MTU reframe events; some of the long tails correlate with reassembly. I recommend testing with jumbo frames disabled on the host NICs as a controlled experiment.

I'll be offline most of the afternoon but pinged infra@brightlane with the pcap and a short summary.

—Aditi

Subject: Re: PrivGPU loadshape profiling + network path inspection

Stephanie / Aditi — I pulled the pcap and did a lightweight path inspection. High-level summary:

- Multiple reassembly events caused by mixed MTU settings between the cloud edge and the host switch (we see 1500 size from user-facing hop, jumbo negotiated internally).
- A handful of SYN retransmits coincide with brief CPU steal on one host (host-10) — NIC counters show RX ring drops during the worst spikes.
- No L7 drops or proxy timeouts in the trace window.

Actionable items I recommend:
- Toggle host MTU to 1500 across the test pool and rerun the 30-minute burst test (simple rollback plan exists).
- Increase RX ring size on host NICs by +25% and enable IRQ balance on the affected hosts.
- For longer term, request BrightLane to disable the passive inspector sampling for the test VLAN during soak windows.

I've attached a short runbook draft with steps to toggle MTU and RX ring sizing (runbook-draft.md). If you want, I can prod infra to do a rolling change on 3 hosts and we can observe the delta.

—Laura
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-draft.md

Quick capacity math after reviewing Laura's notes and the loadshape bins:

- Baseline: 200 sustained inference qps at p95 payload size -> ~120 tokens/req average. On our current private GPU profile (A100x8 equivalent serving partition), network transfer per token adds ~0.6ms median but jumps to 6-10ms in the reassembly tail. Those tails reduce effective token throughput by ~15% under the observed conditions.

- Proposal (short):
  * Primary defense: preventive network tuning (MTU unify to 1500, increase RX rings) — expected to recover ~10% of lost throughput.
  * Compensating scale: raise scale-up threshold to 70% sustained GPU util instead of 60% for burst windows and add a temporary +20% warm pool on expected high-variance days (e.g., new client rollouts). Warm pool is cheaper than overprovisioning permanent capacity.
  * Admission control: implement a per-tenant token-based shed at the edge that favors short LLM flows (small context) during tail events.

If BrightLane can disable sampling during soak runs we should re-run the test with corrected MTU and measure. If tails persist, we should plan a targeted +1 GPU per pod for those noisy subnets.

I'll add these numbers to HB-2374.

—Karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

Thanks all — concise plan to align on tomorrow's sync:

1) BrightLane: disable passive inspector sampling for test VLAN during the 30-minute soak (Aditi to confirm).
2) Infra change window: apply MTU=1500 + RX ring + IRQ balance on three staging hosts (Laura will coordinate).
3) Redwood: run two back-to-back 30-minute soaks — baseline, then after infra change. Karthik will capture p95 token latency and effective token throughput.
4) If tails reduce <5% throughput impact, no permanent capacity change. Else, apply warm-pool +20% (automated), and schedule +1 GPU per pod remediation for affected subnets.

I'll draft a short mutual action plan and attach it to HB-2374. Can everyone review the runbook draft and approve by 10:00am PT tomorrow so infra can book the change window?

Short replies are fine — trying to keep this lean so we can run tests tomorrow.
